## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.

  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.

`econet.add_vacation` and `econet.delete_vacation` services have been removed as downstream dependency (`pyeconet`) removed this functionality.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
- Updating `pyeconet` dependency to fix authentication errors.
- Add config flows.
- Using push for data updates instead of poll.

## Type of change
<!--
  What type of change does your PR introduce to Home Assistant?
  NOTE: Please, check only 1! box!
  If your PR requires multiple boxes to be checked, you'll most likely need to
  split it into multiple PRs. This makes things easier and faster to code review.
-->

- [ ] New integration (thank you!)
- [X] New feature (which adds functionality to an existing integration)

- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

-->

pr_comments: Ready for review. codespell is throwing errors for the package name of `from pyeconet.equipments.water_heater import WaterHeater, WaterHeaterOperationMode`. Anybody know how to ignore this import line for code spell?
Changes look good to me. Eagerly awaiting getting this merged.

@vangorra am testing this as a custom component so far, and things are mostly working. A couple of notes/questions: ``` Logger: homeassistant Source: runner.py:115 First occurred: 10:06:29 PM (2 occurrences) Last logged: 10:06:29 PM Error doing job: Unclosed client session Error doing job: Unclosed connector ``` ``` Logger: custom_components.econet.water_heater Source: custom_components/econet/water_heater.py:105 Integration: Rheem EcoNET Water Products (documentation) First occurred: 10:06:29 PM (1 occurrences) Last logged: 10:06:29 PM Invalid operation mode mapping. WaterHeaterOperationMode.ENERGY_SAVING doesn't map. Please report this. ``` This one seems likely to be downstream in pyeconet CC @w1ll1am23 ``` Logger: pyeconet.equipments.water_heater Source: /usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/pyeconet/equipments/water_heater.py:49 First occurred: 10:06:29 PM (21 occurrences) Last logged: 10:06:29 PM Unknown mode: [Heat Pump ] Unknown mode: [Electric ] Unknown mode: [Vacation ] ``` ![IMG_2622](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/595829/93693201-ad890f80-faca-11ea-9434-ebb6da62c0a0.PNG) Also, how do I set the credentials for this? I got an error message to remove them from my config (which I did), and now see an "Econet" tile in my Integrations tab, which has my email address but no place to set a password? It seems to work though, so maybe it is using a cached token or something?
@vangorra if you are interested in helping maintain the pyeconet library let me know, I have been super busy at work the last 6 months which is why I haven't gotten around to opening this PR myself.

@w1ll1am23 Sure. I'm interested in working on the pyeconet library. 
In regards to vacation modes. While useful independent of Home Assistant, vacation modes are easily replaced by using HASS' automations and provide the user with greater control. I'm all for sticking with the basics and ignoring "features" that HASS handles on it's own.

@vangorra I agree that the vacation functionality can be recreated in Home Assistant. The big problem here is that apparently some units support vacation as a mode. How will Home Assistant handle this? What if the user has vacation mode selected in the app what will HA show? Kinda the same question, but if we enable vacation mode support by using what Home Assistant has built in for away mode we still have the issue of what to show in the operation mode selector.

My unit is one of the ones that has the new "vacation mode"; it shows up as a second "off" entry in the UI and throws an error like this in the log: ``` Logger: custom_components.econet.water_heater Source: custom_components/econet/water_heater.py:105 Integration: Rheem EcoNET Water Products (documentation) First occurred: 10:15:11 PM (1 occurrences) Last logged: 10:15:11 PM Invalid operation mode mapping. WaterHeaterOperationMode.VACATION doesn't map. Please report this. ``` One other issue we're seeing is that we see a "This entity does not have a unique id" error, and no entities show up on the integrations page:
@w1ll1am23 can you rename `equipments` to `equipment` downstream to fix the codespell check that is failing?

> @w1ll1am23 can you rename `equipments` to `equipment` downstream to fix the codespell check that is failing?

Yeah, I guess I can do that. It's named that because that's how their API names it. I'll try to do that later tonight.
Bump the version for pyeconet to 0.1.5 and rename equipments to equipment and you should be good to go.

> Bump the version for pyeconet to 0.1.5 and rename equipments to equipment and you should be good to go.

@vangorra can you make this change in your PR? Should fix the code spell issue.

Fixing the unique_id issue is trivial. Downstream API 0.1.5 is broken. api.py still references pyeconet.equipments.

Support for vacation mode is easy enough to add however pyeconet does not seem to support it yet.

@vangorra sorry about that. I fixed it in 0.1.6.

Vacation is supported as a mode on @appleguru's unit, once we get this MR added we can follow up with another to get that fixed.
@vangorra added my data. Your latest changes look good to me/seem to be working. I think this is good to merge!
@vangorra are you planning to merge this? I think it is good to go other than the vacation issue which can be addressed later.
Almost ready. I'll have time soon

Is there a reason this hasn’t been merged yet? Minor nits aside, the existing integration is 100% broken / does not work today, which this PR fixes.
Please merge ASAP; we can follow on with an additional bug fix/improvement PR as needed.

I agree with @adamurban I've been manually making these merges as homeassistant gets updated and haven't had any issues whatsoever. 

Lets merge this now since it passes all the checks and has no conflicts.
Also agree on this. Existing integration is completely non-functional.
@vangorra Can you make the small fixes above and rename this PR to indicate it fixes a broken integration?

Would just like to add im on  0.115.1   same issue.  

Looks like you guys are working on it already.

New to HA, but have a ProTerra Rheem water heater.
got this today:

ERROR (SyncWorker_5) [pyeconet.api] Authentication request failed, please check credintials. 400
ERROR (SyncWorker_10) [pyeconet.api] Token expired

config is:
```
## RHEEM WATER HEATER
water_heater:
  - platform: econet
    username: !secret rheem_username
    password: !secret rheem_password
```

secrets.yaml contains:
```
rheem_username: '_user@email.address_'
rheem_password: '_password_'
```
```
bash-5.0# cat .HA_VERSION
0.116.2
```

I have nothing in the entities for "econet" or "water*"...etc.
Something I can also add to this is....  I have recently spoken with ECONET support and found out they have shutdown their public facing site where users could previously access/control RHEEM products (econet related).   Unsure if this action has also shutdown some of the API connections?  Might no longer be an API but MQTT now?  This is affecting other platforms like smartthing, hubitat to name a couple.

It looks like the latest version of pyeconet (0.1.6) hasn't been integrated into HA. The requirements documents for HA is installing 0.0.11. The version of pyeconet=0.1.6 looks like it has been updated to work with the new API to econet. The old API was REST based and is now using MQTT_API. 

The Hubitat has an explanation on their community site [here](https://community.hubitat.com/t/release-rheem-econet-integration/37338).
